method: Real offline Cargo fixtures; 65536 bytes/source; warm resolution before seven measured invocations per implementation/size; separate Node bundles of exact git baseline and current source; implementation order alternated by size; taskpolicy background priority, sequential workers. Concurrent host work makes timings noisy.
claim: Ordinary scheduled Rust source reads per invocation fall from two to one. This is not an order-of-magnitude wall-time claim.
crossover: Read-count reduction begins at one source. Timing medians cross between 16 and 64 sources, but 64 is effectively flat (0.14%); 256 is the first measured clearly favorable size. No universal wall-time threshold is inferred.
smallInputRegression: One source: +18.107 ms (+9.51%) median. Sixteen sources: +11.729 ms (+7.21%). These are observed end-to-end fixed-work penalties, not isolated scheduler instruction costs.
retention: Observed live raw source bytes (read completion through hash.update): 65536 before and after at every synthetic size; zero at invocation completion. This does not measure total heap/RSS, decoder strings or token arrays. The scheduler retains only paths and owned UTF-8 literal spellings across sources; no byte cache. Discovery-only sources later named by an include alias may still be read twice.

equivalenceArgument: Unchanged v2 header, symlink block and key/length/bytes framing. File identities still select the same lexical minimum; rekeying retains the original Map insertion ordinal for equal keys.

Within one serialized package identity, ordinary source file keys precede include keys. Emit and scan those bytes first, then integrate the same sorted, deduplicated literal references before emitting include keys. Equal package identities share the boundary.

An earlier identity may include a later package source. It is hashed and scanned at that earlier identity; only owned literal/path metadata is held for its later owner. No later package identity can replace an already emitted smaller key.

Discovery-only files keep synchronous scanning. If an include alias later canonicalizes to one, the original second read supplies the hashed bytes; preserving this exception avoids buffering the workspace.

Graph and runtime discovery share the exact same source traversal and token/literal collector. Only include_str! and include_bytes! remain recognized; UTF-8 round-tripping owns the literal storage without Unicode normalization.
